_doc: 1.10.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T2b, 2026-08-17) — the open is
authored per seat instead of as one number. Before this change the
pack opened 3.0bb with share 1.000 from all eight opening seats, 109
times per 4,000 hands.
Tighter but bigger is correct poker for this seat, and the values say
so. Its off-size rung early is 2.8 rather than the 2.5 the other two
regulars use, and it keeps more mass on 3.0 in late position (0.35
against the tag's 0.12): a player opening few hands and wanting folds
does not shade downward the way a wide opener does. The ladder it
deviates from is still `scenarios._OPEN_SIZE`.
The 3-bet gains a 3.2 rung against a former flat 3.5. Only 20 three-
bets per 4,000 hands, so this is cheap either way; it is authored for
consistency with the other regulars rather than for measured effect.
No 4-bet mix: this pack made zero four-bets in 4,000 hands.
This pack has the least room of the six on the determinism guard — its
share of near-unanimous decision contexts runs 0.148 to 0.178 against
a 0.20 ceiling. Sizing does not enter that statistic, but any later
edit that changes how often the nit acts is measured against those
numbers first. The ledger has them.
Opens stay at or under 3.0 and 3-bet rungs at or under 3.5, both
grading bounds — see the tag's 1.10.0 entry.
[UNVERIFIED] — the weights within each seat, as for every pack in this
ticket.
THIS PACK DELIBERATELY TAKES NO PART in T5's wet-flop fix, and the reason
is measured rather than stylistic. The three regulars needed a third-pot
bet on wet flops between them, because without one that bet named `station
or fish` outright; the tell is a property of the CLASS, so what the fix has
to move is the class's average weight at that cell, and how that average is
split between the three members is a per-persona question. This pack takes
none of it on two grounds that agree. Poker: a nit taking a cheap stab on a
coordinated board is the least characteristic of the three. Measurement:
sizing is not a pure sizing lever — a pack's size mix scales how often it
bluffs (the F2 joint law) — and an 8% third-pot share here cost this pack
2.8% of its wet-flop bluff mass, which took its share of near-unanimous
decision contexts from 17.6% to 21.1% and failed the determinism guard on
one of five seeds. It is the only pack on the roster without the headroom
to spend; the rest sit between 2.9% and 14.0%. The tag and lag carry the
class's whole share instead, at 14% and 16%.
1.9.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T5, 2026-08-16) — postflop bet sizes are
re-weighted so this seat is no longer identifiable by size alone. The
realised bucket table for the whole roster is in the ticket ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) rather than here — see the
tag's 1.8.0 entry for why.
The flat `sizing` block had no 0.33 at all, so a pack that leads out could
never make a small bet; it has one now. `river_value` gains a medium size
for the same reason as the tag's, and the `raise` block was widened at the
same time and that part was wasted — no bot can reach it.
Every value stays on the grader's recognised grid {0.33, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0,
1.5}; nothing is jittered continuously. No 1.5 is authored here — see the
tag's 1.8.0 entry for why an overbet is the one size this slice does not
hand out.
[UNVERIFIED] — no committed source in this repo gives a population
distribution of bet sizes at low-stakes full ring. See the calling
station's 1.7.0 entry for the one sourced observation this is anchored on.
1.8.0 (de-robotization slice 1, 2026-08-15, review rework) — `vs_rfi`,
`vs_limpers` and `vs_3bet` are answered per seat. Facing a raise, the fold
runs 89.64% in the big blind, 93.30% cutoff/button, 94.96% early and 95.17%
in the small blind, against a flat 94.18% before.
That 5.5-point spread is the roster's narrowest in absolute terms and its
WIDEST in relative terms — the big blind continues 2.14x as often as the
small blind and 1.55x as often as the button. Judging a tight range by
percentage points understates it; a nit adjusting less than a lag is the
archetype, and widening it to match would trade one defect for a worse one.
[UNVERIFIED] — per-seat defence targets have no committed source.
1.6.0 (R9-LOOSEFIT rev4, 2026-08-04) — ONE postflop number, `call_looseness`:
0.6 -> 0.45, so the nit folds materially more at facing nodes than it did
and more often than tag wherever the lever reaches (self leg + population
sweep, see docs/ai-dlc/specs/r9-loosefit-rev4.md). `continue_ref` is
DELIBERATELY NOT moved and stays at 0.6 — it is the frozen calibration
anchor the RAISE merit divides by, so re-syncing it with `call_looseness`
would restore the old coupling and delete that feature. `stickiness` is
also untouched at 0.6.
